newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium futures end higher despite dollar.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium futures end higher despite dollar.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures closed higher on Friday, shrugging off the dollar's advance against the yen, traders said.
"We've seen fair amount of buying (by individual investors)," said a trader at one of Japan's leading trading houses. "But the market is likely to remain in a doldrum for the time being."
The June contract added 2.0 yen to finish at 190.7 yen, well above the key 190 yen resistance. The April gained 1.2 yen to 191.6, while others were between down 0.2 and up 1.1 yen.
The rise came in spite of the dollar's retreat to well below 116 yen from above the level.

In London overnight, the benchmark three-month aluminium remained in the recent range, finishing up $4 at $1,574 per tonne, while the flagship copper bounced from five month lows to end up $13 at $2,280.
The Tokyo aluminium market will be closed for a Japanese national holiday on Monday.
